page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance configured with 16 vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. Powered by the x86_64 architecture, the instance operates on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz across 8 physical cores and two threads per core. Memory allocation scales to 4.0 GB per vCPU, supported by 33 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES cryptography instructions. The instance runs under the KVM hypervisor with dedicated CPU core allocation, contains zero bundled local storage, and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or hardware GPUs.

Benchmark testing indicates distinct tradeoffs between single-thread responsiveness and parallel execution. Single-core performance falls in the lower percentile ranges, as reflected in Geekbench single-core results of 906.0 and poor single-threaded compression throughput. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics consistently sit within the median performance bracket. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 17,461.37 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,825.0, demonstrating consistent stability under shared multi-core loads such as Clang compilation, ray tracing, and static web serving reaching 11.07 GB/sec.

In terms of resource density, the configuration provides balanced multi-threaded compute without incurring the overhead of local NVMe arrays or GPU hardware. Uncached memory write bandwidth registers at 47.29 GB/sec alongside uncached read bandwidth of 78.8 GB/sec, producing reliable throughput for concurrent operations such as Redis key-value workloads (measured at 20.14 million operations per second). Given its single-thread limitations, the server is less suited for latency-sensitive serialized execution, functioning best for distributed microservices, standard web hosting, background job queues, and general business databases requiring balanced CPU and memory resources.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n2.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine engineered around an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 hyperthreaded physical cores, paired with 64 GB of system memory at a balanced 1:4 resource ratio. The instance features 33 MB of L3 cache, standard vector extensions, zero attached local storage, and no GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate average multi-core throughput, evident in Clang software compilation and PassMark database processing, alongside high throughput in Redis key-value operations reaching 20.14 million operations per second. However, single-core benchmarks and decompression speeds register in lower percentiles, marking a clear operational tradeoff against serial workloads. The instance is suited for multi-threaded backend services, distributed caching layers, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise databases requiring balanced compute and memory capacity.
